title: Leader-Based Read Path
explain: The read path is about where a read is served and how fresh it has to be. Only the leader is guaranteed to have every committed write, but reads on the leader use the capacity that writes need, so you route each read by how much staleness it can tolerate.
model:
Routing options:

- **Read from the leader:** fresh, but it caps read throughput.
- **Read from a follower:** scales reads, but data may be stale by the replication lag.
- **Route by need:** reads that feed a decision, or that follow the user's own write, go to the leader (or a caught-up follower); the rest go to followers.

Techniques:

```
write ─▶ returns log position 812
read  ─▶ follower with applied_position ≥ 812 ? serve : wait / fall back to leader
```

- **Position-tagged reads:** carry the write's log position and require the follower to have applied at least that.
- **Lag-aware routing:** drop followers whose lag exceeds a threshold from the read pool.
- **Sticky routing:** pin a user to one follower so reads do not go backwards.
- **A leader read is not automatically fresh:** a deposed leader that does not know it was replaced can serve stale data, so linearizable reads need a leadership check (a [lease](#/sd/f/lease) or a quorum round).

The guarantees these give are in [leader-based consistency](#/sd/f/leader-based-consistency); the write side is the [write path](#/sd/f/leader-based-write-path). A [read/write replica split](#/sd/f/rw-replicas) is the usual deployment.

details.q: Which reads should still go to the leader in a shopping app?
details.a: Reads that feed a decision (stock check at checkout, balance before a charge) and reads right after the user's own write (their cart, their order). Browsing, product pages and feeds can use followers.

details.q: How many followers do I need for 18,000 reads/s if one node serves 5,000 and the leader serves none?
details.a: 18,000 / 5,000 = 3.6, so 4 followers, ignoring headroom. In practice add spare capacity so that one failed follower does not overload the others.

details.q: A follower is 8 s behind and my freshness budget is 2 s. What should the router do?
details.a: Take it out of the read pool until it catches up (lag-aware routing), and send its traffic to healthy followers or the leader. Alert if many followers exceed the budget.

details.q: An old leader is partitioned and a new one has been elected. A client still reaches the old one. Is its data fresh?
details.a: No. It does not know it has been replaced and may serve stale reads. Linearizable reads need a leadership check: a lease that it verifies is still valid, or a quorum round.

details.q: How does a position-tagged read give read-your-writes?
details.a: The write returns its log position; the next read carries it; the router sends the read to a follower whose applied position is at least that, or waits briefly, or falls back to the leader.
Two consecutive reads from different followers with different lag can show newer data and then older data. Pinning a session to one follower makes its view move only forward.

prompts.q: List three read-routing policies for a leader-based store and the staleness each allows.
points: Any follower: scalable, stale by replication lag
Route by need or position token: fresh where it matters

prompts.q: Explain how you give a user read-your-writes without sending all reads to the leader.
points: Write returns a log position or version
Read is sent with that position
Follower serves only if it has applied it
Otherwise wait briefly or use the leader
Short window of leader reads is a simpler fallback

prompts.q: Explain why reading from the leader is not always fresh.
points: Leader may have been deposed by a partition
It does not know it was replaced
Need a lease or quorum confirmation
Fencing for writes, lease check for reads
